issues.legal_issue: A suit for possession against a person occupying bhumidhari land without title must be brought in the special court designated by statute, rather than an ordinary civil court.
material_facts: The plaintiffs claimed title as the next reversioners to bhumidhari plots and alleged that the defendant was occupying the plots without title.
The suit sought an injunction and, alternatively, possession, but was filed in an ordinary civil court.
The courts found that the plaintiffs had title and that the defendant had none.
issues.conclusion: The suit fell within the statutory ejectment procedure, and the ordinary civil court had no jurisdiction to entertain it; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 209 and 331 of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1951, read together with Schedule II, item 24, required a suit for ejectment of a person occupying land without title to be filed in the designated Assistant Collector court and barred ordinary civil courts from taking cognizance of it. The applicable limitation period was the one prescribed under the Rules made under the Act. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.possession_suit_for_unauthorized_occupat: The proceeding is a suit seeking possession of bhumidhari land from a person alleged to occupy it without title.
predicates.statute_assigns_ejectment_suit_to_specia: The governing statutory scheme assigns this kind of ejectment suit to a specially designated court.
predicates.ordinary_court_jurisdiction_is_excluded: The governing statutory scheme excludes ordinary civil courts from hearing this kind of suit.

issues.definition: When a possession suit concerns unauthorized occupation of bhumidhari land and the statutory scheme assigns it to a special court while excluding ordinary courts, the ordinary civil court lacks jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: An objection that a court inherently lacked jurisdiction may be raised at any stage, including in proceedings to execute its decree.
material_facts: The defendant did not challenge the civil court's jurisdiction in the courts below.
The jurisdictional objection was considered in the Supreme Court appeal.
Counsel for the plaintiffs conceded that an inherent jurisdictional defect could be raised even in execution proceedings on the ground that the decree was a nullity.
issues.conclusion: An objection based on an inherent lack of jurisdiction may be raised at any stage, including in execution proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: A court's inherent lack of jurisdiction may be raised at any stage because a decree made without jurisdiction is a nullity; the Court cited no earlier cases for this proposition.

predicates.appeal_challenges_decree_of_civil_court: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decree made by a civil court.
predicates.court_inherently_lacked_jurisdiction: The civil court lacked jurisdiction over the kind of suit it entertained.
predicates.jurisdiction_objection_was_not_raised_ea: The jurisdictional objection was not raised in the lower courts.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a civil court decree, the court inherently lacked jurisdiction, and no earlier jurisdictional objection was raised, the objection can still be raised at any stage.
